thread.document:
I have a curiosity-driven question about Deep Learning as a subject and field of human endeavor. 

For the final project, our team utilized LoRA to train models from the start instead of doing just fine-tuning. Over the course of developing the background section of our project, we found various refinements on the LoRA algorithm that have been produced. Out of curiosity, are there any recent training or fine-tuning algorithms from papers that you would be willing to share below with the rest of the class?

answers.document:
On the topic of refinements of LoRA, some related work are:

1. Better performance under the same LoRA budget

LoRA+: uses different learning rates for A and B, and shows this improves training for width-scaling (embedding dimension/ MLP dimension in transformers). https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.12354

2. More parameter-efficient use of rank

AdaLoRA: instead of picking one fixed rank everywhere, it tries to allocate rank where it matters so you get more mileage out of the same (or smaller) parameter budget. https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.10512

3. Other memory bottleneck rather than parameter count

QLoRA: not really “fewer LoRA params”, but a practical recipe for making large-model fine-tuning fit on limited GPUs (quantize the frozen base model to low-bit, then train LoRA adapters). Perhaps one of the most popular ones right now. https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.14314

4. When does LoRA actually match full fine-tuning?

There’s also the “LoRA Without Regret” blog (Thinking Machines) that does a helpful empirical study on when LoRA can match full FT (and when it predictably won’t), depending on things like data size / how many trainable adapter params you give it and practical findings like attention-only LoRA underperforming relative to applying LoRA broadly (eg including MLP/MoE). https://thinkingmachines.ai/blog/lora/
